felix: Heads-up — ran the paged-attn perf suite on prod-sim and hit OOMs after the kernel-selector bump. stack traces + small dump below.

aj: which selector change? the matmul heuristic or the workspace priming?

felix: matmul heuristic + we enabled dynamic workspace sizing by default (opt-in -> opt-out). Repro steps:
```
# run repro
./run_perf.sh --model rl-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --paged-attn
kubectl logs -c runtime inference-rl-13b-0 --tail=200
```

jorge: paste of the hottest lines from the pod log:
```
E GPU_OOM: failed allocation 1.2GB at blockmgr->alloc_block(): workspace_needed=1.8GB, free=900MB
W kernel_selector: fallback from matmul_opt to generic_gemm for layer 5
I kv_cache: page eviction triggered, evicted=12 blocks (48MB), compaction_cost=0.34s
```

tanya: interesting — eviction occurred *after* kernel fallback. that suggests the kernel path enlarged temporary workspace size, not the base block footprint.

aj: initial thought: matmul_opt uses fused buffers + staging that double-peaks memory occasionally. dynamic workspace sizing may have chosen a too-aggressive guard.

perf-bot: quick capture from perf profiler (single trace):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY
seq_len=2048 batch=1
layer 5: kernel=matmul_opt ws_alloc=1.1GB time=3.2ms
layer 5: fallback=generic_gemm ws_alloc=450MB time=5.6ms
block_reuse_hits=18 block_allocs=24 compaction_ops=3
```

felix: so matmul_opt is faster but requires ~2.4x more temporary workspace at peak in our workload. When it falls back, it frees some temporaries but we still see blocks pinned by KV cache and fragmentation.

jorge: can we try: (1) reduce matmul_opt's peak workspace by switching to tiled-kernel variant, (2) add a soft cap for dynamic workspace (< 75% of free) so we don't greedily claim.

aj: I prototyped a small heuristic yesterday: if dynamic_workspace > free*0.75 then degrade to tiled-kernel. quick pseudo:
```
if requested_workspace > free_memory * 0.75:
    kernel = tiled_matmul
else:
    kernel = matmul_opt
```

tanya: also worth measuring fragmentation: current block manager splits pages into 16MB blocks. For long-tail seqs the tail blocks are cold but keep small holes when we evict. Maybe increase block size for paged-attn (to 32MB) to reduce per-block metadata and compaction cost. tradeoff: increased internal waste.

felix: I pushed a canary that: switches to tiled kernel on workspace pressure + increases block size to 24MB for paged-attn models. Running canary now.

infra-bot: deploy canary to staging (canary-id=rl-13b-2026-03-18-01).

aj: quick perf snapshot from the canary run (seq 2048, batch 1):
```
CANARY SNAP
kernel=tiled_matmul ws_peak=820MB time=3.9ms (-18% vs generic fallback)
block_size=24MB block_reuse_hits=21 compactions=1
OOMs=0 (prev=3)
```

jorge: good signal — latency slightly up vs matmul_opt but way better than fallback and no OOMs. compaction_count down which reduces CPU jitter.

tanya: follow-ups:
- add telemetry to record workspace_request vs actual_alloc and the reason for kernel fallback (workspace_limit|compatibility)
- try an adaptive block size: start 24MB, if reuse_hits<10 increase to 32MB for next run
- verify effect on Dedicated instances (higher mem pressure)

felix: agreed. I'll file an RFC for: kernel fallback policy + workspace soft-cap + adaptive block sizing. will include perf plots and the canary snapshot.

aj: small immediate mitigation we can flip if needed: revert dynamic_workspace default to previous safe limit (opt-in).

perf-bot: note added to traces: tag=kernel_fallback_reason workspace_pressure=true kv_compaction=observed

felix: thanks all — leaving the canary run for a few hours, will update thread with numbers. @tanya @jorge ping me if you want to pair on the RFC.
